overview: This enum chooses the unit vector used as the base direction of a hit.

None.technical: The header defines None as the zero value and the Damage row constructor uses it as the default. CalcHitDirection has no case for None, so the incoming direction remains unchanged before pitch and yaw adjustments. The incoming direction is normally the zero vector when the request has no earlier direction.

AttackerDirection.simple: The hit travels the way the attacker faces.
AttackerDirection.technical: CalcHitDirection assigns Attacker->GetFacingForwardVector() when the attacker pointer is valid. The selected vector then receives the row pitch and yaw corrections.

ReceiverDirection.simple: The hit travels the way the target faces.
ReceiverDirection.technical: CalcHitDirection assigns Receiver->GetFacingForwardVector() when the receiver pointer is valid. The selected vector then receives the row pitch and yaw corrections.

AttackerToReceiver.simple: The hit travels from the attacker toward the target.
AttackerToReceiver.technical: CalcHitDirection normalizes receiver location minus attacker location when both pointers are valid. When that vector is nearly zero or nearly vertical, the fallback normalizes receiver location plus attacker forward minus attacker location.

ActorDirection.simple: The hit travels the way the damage instigator faces.
ActorDirection.technical: CalcHitDirection assigns the instigator actor forward vector when the instigator weak pointer is valid. The instigator is separate from the attacker and is often an effect or trap actor.

ActorToReceiver.simple: The hit travels from the damage instigator toward the target.
ActorToReceiver.technical: CalcHitDirection normalizes receiver location minus instigator location when both are valid. When that vector is nearly zero or nearly vertical, the fallback normalizes receiver location minus receiver forward minus instigator location.

MovementDirection.simple: The hit travels the way the attacker is moving.
MovementDirection.technical: CalcHitDirection assigns Attacker->GetMoveDelta().GetSafeNormal() when the attacker pointer is valid. GetSafeNormal returns a zero vector for a tiny move delta.

Invalid.technical: The header defines Invalid as the explicit 255 sentinel. No traced branch names Invalid, so it takes the same default path as None. No exported Damage row uses this value.

notes: Every selected vector is adjusted afterward by DamageDirectionAdjustPitch and DamageDirectionAdjustYaw, and bIgnoreDamageDirectionPitch removes the vertical component first.
The nearly vertical and nearly zero fallback tests use KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER and apply only to AttackerToReceiver and ActorToReceiver.
No aliases or unused numeric slots appear between None and Invalid.
